title: Beyond the 956: Irma P. Hall, Soul Food's beloved Big Mama, dies at 91
excerpt: Irma P. Hall, the Texas schoolteacher turned award-winning actress best known as Big Mama in Soul Food, died November 10, 2026, in Dallas. She was 91. Her family announced her death on November 11.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Irma P. Hall, the Texas schoolteacher who became one of American film's most beloved matriarchs as Big Mama in Soul Food, has died at 91.

Hall died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Dallas, surrounded by her loved ones, her family announced in a statement on Wednesday, November 11. No cause of death was disclosed, and the family asked for privacy as they grieve. Details about memorial services will be announced later.

Born Irma Dolores Player on June 3, 1935, in Beaumont, Texas, Hall grew up in Chicago and returned to Texas to attend college. She spent 27 years teaching high school in Texas before acting found her: director Raymond St. Jacques cast her in his 1973 film Book of Numbers after hearing her read poetry.

Her breakthrough came in the 1990s. She played Aunt T in A Family Thing (1996) opposite Robert Duvall and James Earl Jones, then won an NAACP Image Award as Josephine “Big Mama Joe” Joseph, the matriarch holding a Chicago family together at the Sunday dinner table in Soul Food (1997). She reprised the role in the television series, and her performance inspired Boyz II Men's song “A Song for Mama.”

Hall went on to star opposite Tom Hanks in the Coen brothers' The Ladykillers (2004), which won the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival, and appeared with Tom Cruise in Collateral (2004). She founded the Dallas Minority Repertory Theatre and was inducted into the Texas Film Hall of Fame.

Tom Hanks paid tribute to his Ladykillers co-star after her death. Hall is survived by her daughter, Irma Hall Crayton.

Sources: People; USA Today; Variety; TV Insider; statement from the family of Irma P. Hall.
